Celebrations

Chestnut and apple cake

Gesztenyetorta

12 months+ Replaced 50 min 8 portions

Offer it occasionally from 12 months. Chestnut does not stand in for walnut or peanut, so practise those nuts in their own foods once each is tolerated.

Freezes well.

Ingredients

  • 200 g peeled chestnuts (boiled until completely soft; not a walnut or peanut)
  • 1 large eating apple (peeled and cooked soft)
  • 50 g plain wheat flour (just enough to hold a single soft cake)
  • 1 tbsp rapeseed or olive oil (no chocolate and no sugar)

Allergens

gluten

Method

  1. Boil the peeled chestnuts until they mash with no firm bits, then drain them.
  2. Cook the peeled, chopped apple in a splash of water until it collapses.
  3. Mash the chestnuts and apple with the oil.
  4. Stir in the flour and spread the soft batter in one small tin.
  5. Bake at 180 C until the middle is set and still soft.
  6. Cool, then cut a small piece.

Replaced

Chocolate chestnut cakes are a sweet.

This is the edible version: cooked peeled chestnut and apple baked with a little oil and flour into a single soft cake, with no chocolate and no sugar. Chestnut is not the same as introducing walnut or peanut.
